x: The jajmani system, linking service castes to landholding patrons, is traced to the post-Gupta period. It does not belong to the Satavahana, Gupta or Mauryan periods.

Khadar, the new alluvium renewed by floods every year, is the most fertile land. Bhabar (printed key) is a porous belt of pebbles and boulders where streams vanish, the least fertile; Bhangar is older alluvium with kankar.

from_notes: Silk weaving | Lata (Gujarat), until the weavers moved to Mandsaur (Malwa)
x: Gujarat, Bengal, the Deccan and the Tamil country were centres of textile manufacture, and textiles were the main Gupta export. Gems and opium are not linked with all these centres.

from_notes: "NOT a feature of guilds" – the answer is always "non-autonomous bodies"
x: Gupta guilds were autonomous bodies with their own laws, judicial powers and even armed bodies. So 'non-autonomous bodies' is the feature they did not have.
source: APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:5:7; PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-03.pdf) p.67

from_notes: Mandsaur composer is Vatsabhatti – not Bhava / Bhavabhuti (MPPSC 2021, 2024).
x: The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti, not Bhavabhuti, so option 4 is incorrect. It does record the Sun temple, praises silk cloth (oldest advertisement) and calls Dashpur Pashchimapur.
source: Rocket Indian History 01 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.pdf) p.85; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:5:10

from_notes: Dashpur / Mandsaur (Kumaragupta I, governor Bandhuvarman) | Silk-weavers' guild (Tantuwayas) from Lata built a Sun temple
x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription records the silk weavers' guild that built and repaired a Sun temple. The Prayag, Eran and Hathigumpha records do not.

from_notes: Oldest advertisement tradition in India – Dashpur inscription
x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription of Kumaragupta I's time, praising silk cloth, is called the first advertisement. Sohgaura, Supia and Eran are other records.

from_notes: Tamralipti (Tamluk) | Bengal, east coast | Chief port for North Indian trade
x: Tamralipti (Tamluk, Bengal) handled the trade of northern India in the Gupta period. Broach, Kalyan and Cambay were western ports.
source: Rocket Indian History 01 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.pdf) p.64; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:6:0.0

from_notes: UPSC 2020: Ghantasala, Kadura and Chaul handled foreign trade.
x: Ghantasala and Kadura (Andhra coast) and Chaul (Konkan) were ports handling foreign trade. They were not capitals, art sites or pilgrim centres.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-04.pdf) p.142; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:6:3

from_notes: UPSC 2020: Ghantasala, Kadura and Chaul handled foreign trade.
x: Ghantasala, Kadura and Chaul were ports handling foreign trade in the Gupta period. None was a royal capital or a Buddhist pilgrim centre.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-04.pdf) p.142; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:6:3

from_notes: Tamralipti (Tamluk) | Bengal, east coast | Chief port for North Indian trade
x: Tamralipti, on the east coast, handled North Indian trade in the Gupta period. Kalyan, Broach and Cambay were western ports.
source: Rocket Indian History 01 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.pdf) p.64; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:6:0.0

from_notes: Tamralipti (Tamluk) | Bengal, east coast | Chief port for North Indian trade
x: Tamralipti in Bengal was the port for North Indian trade with SE Asia, China and Lanka. Bhadoch (Broach), Kalyan and Cambay served the west coast.
source: Rocket Indian History 01 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.pdf) p.64; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:6:0.0

from_notes: Declining towns: Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti, Kaushambi ... "Towns declined only by the mid-9th century" is false.
x: The decline of sites like Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti and Kaushambi and the paucity of coins are true (b, c). The decline was marked from the 6th-7th century, not only by the mid-9th, so a is false.
source: APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:8:7-10; PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-03.pdf) p.68

from_notes: Fall of the West Roman Empire | Standard cause of North Indian trade decline (APPSC G2 2017)
x: The collapse of the West Roman Empire cut the long-distance trade on which North India had prospered. China and SE Asia did not collapse, and artisans' skills did not decline.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-03.pdf) p.68; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:8:1.1

from_notes: Gradual decline of towns = feature of the Gupta period
x: The gradual decline of towns is a feature of the Gupta period: Mathura, Hastinapur, Shravasti declined and Pataliputra became a village by Hiuen-Tsang's time. The other eras are not marked by it.
source: APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:8:7-8; NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 (src/indian-history/nextgen-indian-history-appsc-03.pdf) p.6

from_notes: After the fall of Rome, merchants relied more on South-East Asian trade via Tamralipti
x: With the Roman market lost, Indian merchants turned more to South-East Asian trade. African, West European and Middle Eastern trade did not replace it.
source: APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 64:8:3; NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 (src/indian-history/nextgen-indian-history-appsc-03.pdf) p.7

from_notes: Gradual decline of towns = feature of the Gupta period
x: The gradual decline of towns is a recognised feature of the Gupta period, with Mathura, Hastinapur and Kaushambi declining. The Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Satavahana eras are not characterised this way.
Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.
The Kaustubha gem, which rose from the churning of the ocean, adorns Vishnu's chest. Marakatham (emerald), Manikyam (ruby) and Pagadam (coral) are ordinary gems.
Indra's thunderbolt, the Vajrayudha, was made from the backbone of sage Dadhichi to kill Vritra. Pashupata was Shiva's weapon, Brahmastra Brahma's and Gandiva Arjuna's bow.

At the exam the latest Jnanpith (52nd, for 2016) had gone to Bengali poet Shankha Ghosh (now: the 60th, for 2025, went to Tamil poet R. Vairamuthu, announced 14 March 2026). Raghuveer Chaudhari won for 2015, Kedarnath Singh for 2013 and Pratibha Ray for 2011.

from_notes: First worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna = the Bhagavatas (Vasudevaks) (UPPSC 1997); the name is known in Panini's age.
x: The Bhagavatas (Vasudevakas) were the first worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, known from Panini's time. Vedic Aryans worshipped nature gods, and the Tamils and Abhiras are not credited with it.

from_notes: Gupta rulers patronized Bhagvatism, centered around the worship of Bhagvat (Vishnu) and his incarnations.
x: Bhagavatism peaked under the Guptas, who made it virtually the state religion and styled themselves Parama Bhagavata with Garuda as emblem. Indo-Greeks like Heliodorus were only early patrons.
source: NextGen Indian History APPSC 03 (src/indian-history/nextgen-indian-history-appsc-03.pdf) p.9; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 65:1:9

from_notes: Earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism = Garuda pillar at Besnagar (Vidisha).
x: The Besnagar Garuda pillar of Heliodorus (2nd c. BCE) is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. The Prayag prashasti, Nasik and Ayodhya records are later.

from_notes: Dashavatara: Ten avatars of Vishnu (in sequence) includes – Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha
x: In the Varaha (boar) avatar Vishnu killed Hiranyaksha and lifted the Earth from the cosmic ocean on his tusks. Matsya saved Manu from the flood, Kurma bore Mount Mandara and Narasimha killed Hiranyakashipu.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-03.pdf) p.71; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 65:1:15

from_notes: Earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism = Garuda pillar at Besnagar (Vidisha).
x: The Garuda column at Besnagar, set up by the Greek envoy Heliodorus, is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. Samudragupta's Prayag prashasti is much later.

from_notes: Centre of worship: Vasudeva-Krishna (son of Devaki) of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan.
x: The Bhagavata religion goes back to Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan, son of Devaki. Janaka and Yajnavalkya are Upanishadic figures and Surdas a medieval poet.

from_notes: Kalika Purana (Kali / Sati Purana) – Shaktism; an upapurana, likely written in Assam
x: The Kalika Purana is an upapurana of the Shakta (goddess) tradition, probably composed in Assam. It is not Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain.

from_notes: Kalika Purana (Kali / Sati Purana) – Shaktism; an upapurana, likely written in Assam
x: The Kalika Purana belongs to Shaktism, the worship of the goddess. It is not a Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain text.

from_notes: They worship Lord Shiva in the form of Bhairav, a formidable figure.
x: Kapalini, the skull-bearing form of the goddess consort of Kapali-Bhairava, was worshipped by the Kapalikas. Kalika is a goddess, not a sect, and the Shaktas and Vaishnavas are broader traditions.
Sonam Wangchuk of Ladakh received the Ramon Magsaysay Award 2018 (with Bharat Vatwani). T.M. Krishna won it in 2016, and Anshu Gupta and Sanjiv Chaturvedi in 2015.

from_notes: Gunaga Vijayaditya embraced Shaivism and built Shiva temples at Bikkavolu
x: Saivism dominated under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: kings built Shiva temples (Biccavolu, Draksharama), and Buddharamas became Saiva shrines. Jainism and Buddhism declined.
Mammals (and amphibians) have a dicondylic skull, joined to the vertebral column by two occipital condyles. Reptiles and birds have a monocondylic skull.

Gupta-period temples survive at Bhitargaon (brick temple, Kanpur), Deogarh (Dashavatara) and Bhitari (Ghazipur, Skandagupta's excavated Vishnu temples). Rajgir is known for Buddhist and earlier Magadhan sites, not a Gupta temple.

from_notes: The Kapalikas emerged from the school of Misra Saivam
x: The NextGen APPSC fact list states that the Kapalikas emerged from the Misra Saivam school, which is the APPSC key. Pashupata is the oldest Shaiva sect, and Vaishnavam is a different tradition.
source: NextGen AP History 06 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-06.pdf) p.14; APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 65:3:0.1

from_notes: Mattamayura | Found in Chedi inscriptions
x: Mattamayura was a Shaiva sect known from Chedi (Kalachuri) inscriptions. The Ajivikas were a heterodox sect, Mayamata is an architecture text and Isanasivagurudeva Paddhati a ritual manual.

from_notes: Ardhanarishvara = union of Shiva and Parvati (Shaivism + Shaktism).
x: Ardhanarishvara, half Shiva and half Parvati, shows the god united with his Shakti. 'Union of male and female' and 'god and goddess' are looser versions of the same idea.

Serena Williams beat Angelique Kerber of Germany in the 2016 Wimbledon women's singles final, her 22nd Grand Slam title. Muguruza had beaten Serena in the 2015 final, and Venus won the doubles with her.

from_notes: Gunaga Vijayaditya embraced Shaivism and built Shiva temples at Bikkavolu
x: Hinduism (Saivism, Vaishnavism), Buddhism and Jainism all existed under the Chalukyas, but Judaism had no place in their realm. So Judaism was the religion not prevalent.
Nandi is Shiva's bull (3), Kalpavriksha the divine tree (4), Airavata the divine white elephant (1) and Kamadhenu the holy cow (2), giving 3-4-1-2.

from_notes: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh near Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh depicts Vishnu's ten avatars.
x: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh is a Gupta temple (c. 6th c. CE) of the early Nagara style, depicting Vishnu's ten avatars. The Pallavas, Cholas and Vijayanagara built in the south and later.

from_notes: Panchayatan: A style of temple construction
x: Panchayatana is a style of temple construction with the main shrine and four subsidiary shrines. It is not a village assembly, sect or office.

from_notes: Panchayatan: A style of temple construction
x: Panchayatana is a temple plan with a central shrine and four subsidiary shrines, as at Deogarh. It is not an assembly, a sect or a functionary.

from_notes: Earliest Panchayatana = Dashavatara temple, Deogarh (Lalitpur, near Jhansi) ... Garhwa fort (Shankargarh, Prayagraj) – Gupta temple complex and sculptures.
x: The Deogarh temple near Jhansi and the Garhwa sculptures near Allahabad are remains of Gupta art. The Mauryas built no such temples and the Rashtrakutas worked in the Deccan.
source: APPSC Complete app notes (old-notes.txt) 65:9:5-6; PMF Ancient & Medieval 03 (src/indian-history/pmf-ancient-medieval-03.pdf) p.76
